P1.evidence: Frame delivered twice because the first attempt was lost to the connection, and both times it was the same three parts: "go into where you're currently at, where you want to go, see if we can help you. If we can, perfect, I'll take you through how. If not, also perfectly fine, I'll point you in the right direction." No 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement taken ("okay, Jacob?" / "Exactly. Perfect.") and the open question run as written. The application was used later in the call ("I saw that you also noted down that you want to make sure that your mobility is going to get better") rather than read back at the open.

P2.evidence: Strong on the four things he did ask: the injury screen was direct and produced the wrist history ("do you have any sort of aches, pains, any sort of injuries that I should know of?"), current training and structure were established, progress from current effort was checked ("do you feel like you're actually gaining weight at the moment or is it quite stationary?"), and nutrition was worked properly including tracking and eating window. Against that: age was never asked and is still unknown; height and weight only arrived because the prospect volunteered them while describing his goal; occupation was never asked despite him mentioning night work unprompted; health conditions were never asked as a category; and sleep and energy were both skipped, which on a night-shift worker is the most costly omission in the baseline.

P3.evidence: The why question was asked well and in the ICP's own language: "so many people who are in your position... they would be like, oh, this is perfect for me. What's your why for wanting to step up instead of being good, go to being the best for yourself?" It produced the whole call in one answer — the newborn, stopping drinking and partying, wanting to be the role model. The reflect-back was genuinely good: "The weight increase, the more mobility aspect, that's all more of a by-product for you... it's the mental part, getting back into the state you were in when you were in the army." But the impact on others was volunteered rather than asked for, and the drive through to what fatherhood actually means was interrupted by the connection and never resumed.

P4.evidence: Past attempts asked directly and well framed — "why did you decide to go for kettlebells, instead of doing what you exactly know how to do, go to the gym?" — which produced the real barrier: "I never liked the gym... too many people, too many movements, too many hours." The follow-up 'why did you stop going to the gym when your partner got pregnant' was asked and the answer was lost entirely to a connection drop, and the rep rescheduled rather than re-asking it. The gap was never named and the root-cause challenge was never reached.

P5.evidence: Call terminated at 00:18:19 by the rep for connection quality, before the consequence frame. Not reachable.

P6.evidence: Not reached. No presentation and no commitment check; the call was rescheduled to Saturday.

P11.evidence: No close attempted. No price was ever mentioned.

notes: Only twenty minutes of discovery survive, and within them the goals work was the best-framed of the batch — the 'why step up from good' question is well-tuned to an already-lean prospect and it opened him immediately. The reusable coaching point is the decision to stop: the rep chose to reschedule rather than present into a broken connection, which is the right call and should be reinforced. Baseline discipline is the weakness that carries across every call in this batch — age, occupation and sleep were all skipped again.
